title: Finite compact-support reduction transitions have the specified invertible tensor adjoint
statement:
Fix a field $k$, a prime $\ell$ invertible in $k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and positive integers $m\geq n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes, $f:X\to Y$ separated of finite type, and $c=(j,p)$ a fixed compactification [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For $T=X,Y$ use its small pro-etale site and let $B_{T,s}=(R/\varpi^s)_T$ for $s=m,n$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $D_T(B_{T,s})=D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_{T,s}))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $\operatorname{Res}_T:D_T(B_{T,n})\to D_T(B_{T,m})$ for quotient scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], $L_T=-\otimes^L_{B_{T,m}}B_{T,n}$ for derived scalar extension, and $\eta_T$ for the unit of $L_T\dashv\operatorname{Res}_T$ [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Put $F_s=Rp_{*,s}j_!$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and use the canonical comparison $\sigma:F_m\operatorname{Res}_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_YF_n$ [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. Let $V\in D_X(B_{X,m})$ and $W\in D_X(B_{X,n})$ be intrinsically bounded constructible [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], and let $\beta:L_XV\xrightarrow{\sim}W$ be an isomorphism. Put $\rho=\operatorname{Res}_X(\beta)\eta_{X,V}$ and $\tau=\sigma_WF_m(\rho)$.

Let $\gamma_V:L_YF_mV\to F_nL_XV$ be the canonical compact-support tensor comparison of [def-coef-compact-support-tensor-comparison], characterized by $\operatorname{Res}_Y(\gamma_V)\eta_{Y,F_mV}=\sigma_{L_XV}F_m(\eta_{X,V})$. Then the tensor/restriction adjoint of the actual map $\tau$ is exactly $F_n(\beta)\gamma_V$; equivalently,
$$\operatorname{Res}_Y(F_n(\beta)\gamma_V)\eta_{Y,F_mV}=\sigma_WF_m(\rho).$$
Both $\gamma_V$ and $F_n(\beta)$ are isomorphisms. This assertion concerns ordinary finite-level derived scalar extension and imposes no flatness of $R/\varpi^n$ over $R/\varpi^m$ and no Tor-amplitude hypothesis.

proof.text: For every integer $q$, the isomorphism $\beta:L_XV\xrightarrow{\sim}W$ induces $\mathcal H^q(L_XV)\cong\mathcal H^q(W)$. Thus the same finite cohomological support and the same finite stratifications with locally constant finite module stalks that witness intrinsic bounded constructibility of $W$ witness it for $L_XV$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. In particular the actual ordinary derived reduction of $V$, not a separately chosen reduction object, satisfies the bounded-constructible hypothesis needed below. In Lean, apply the isomorphism-closure clause of [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated] to beta inverse, using the definition of intrinsic bounded constructibility.

source.place: Paragraph 2, input finite coefficient maps; verification of the bounded actual reduction

proof.text: Apply [lem-finite-compact-support-scalar-comparison] with ground field $K_0=k$, input $K=V$, upper level $m$ and lower level $n$, and the given compactification $c$. Its hypotheses are exactly $\ell$ invertible in $k$, positive $n\le m$, separated finite-type $f$ between finite-type $k$-schemes, bounded constructibility of $V$, and bounded constructibility of its actual reduction $L_XV$ from Step 1. The theorem makes the scalar-adjunction transpose of $\sigma_{L_XV}F_m(\eta_{X,V})$ invertible. By [def-coef-compact-support-tensor-comparison], this is precisely $\gamma_V$: both are the unique arrow mapped to that same composite by the tensor-presentation Hom bijection. Hence $\gamma_V$ is an isomorphism. The cited theorem imposes no flatness or Tor-amplitude condition.

proof.text:
Use the defining equation for $\gamma_V$ [def-coef-compact-support-tensor-comparison] and naturality in the argument of the specified restriction comparison [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. Naturality at the $B_{X,n}$-linear arrow $\beta:L_XV\to W$ reads $\operatorname{Res}_Y(F_n(\beta))\sigma_{L_XV}=\sigma_WF_m(\operatorname{Res}_X(\beta))$. Therefore, using functoriality and associativity,
$$\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Res}_Y(F_n(\beta)\gamma_V)\eta_{Y,F_mV}&=\operatorname{Res}_Y(F_n(\beta))\operatorname{Res}_Y(\gamma_V)\eta_{Y,F_mV}\\&=\operatorname{Res}_Y(F_n(\beta))\sigma_{L_XV}F_m(\eta_{X,V})\\&=\sigma_WF_m(\operatorname{Res}_X(\beta))F_m(\eta_{X,V})\\&=\sigma_WF_m(\operatorname{Res}_X(\beta)\eta_{X,V})=\sigma_WF_m(\rho)=\tau.\end{aligned}$$

source.place: Paragraph 2, identification of the specified coefficient maps; expansion of the tensor-unit defining equation and restriction naturality

proof.text: The scalar adjunction of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] sends an arrow $a:L_YF_mV\to F_nW$ to $\operatorname{Res}_Y(a)\eta_{Y,F_mV}$. Step 3 and injectivity of this Hom bijection show that the adjoint of the actual $\tau$ is exactly $F_n(\beta)\gamma_V$. Finally $F_n(\beta)$ has inverse $F_n(\beta^{-1})$, since the two composites are $F_n(1)=1$. It is therefore an isomorphism, and together with Step 2 this proves both claimed invertibilities (and the invertibility of their composite).
